title: bug: scripts/tests/runtime-requirements.test.mjs "Docker CI smoke match has exit 0" times out at the tip (spawnSync /bin/bash ETIMEDOUT at 10 s), because 291a34e3 appended a docker run -d / docker port / curl /health poll to docker.yml's Test Docker image step and the test's docker stub answers only `run`, so CI's "Test installers with isolated profiles" step is red on every OS leg
description:
Filed by hunt #20 (task-9f3eac6d, a CI dry run of moe/work-2026-10-24 at bc4793cf).

PROBLEM
- `.github/workflows/docker.yml:71-113`, step "Test Docker image". 291a34e3 (task-90ed6cb5, DONE, 2026-11-03 21:44) appended a health check after the version check, at lines 82-113:
  - `docker run -d --name "$name" ... -p 127.0.0.1::9876`;
  - `port=$(docker port "$name" 9876/tcp | head -n 1)`;
  - a 30-try loop of `curl -fsS -m 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"` with `sleep 1`;
  - a node check that /health reports `status: healthy` and `projectPath: $PWD`;
  - `docker exec` of the image's HEALTHCHECK.
- `scripts/tests/runtime-requirements.test.mjs:38-60` replays that step's `run:` block with `bash -e` (spawnSync, `timeout: 10000`). Its `docker` stub (:28-36) answers only `docker run`, by printing the version in match mode.
- So in match mode the version check passes and the script continues into the new block:
  - `docker port` prints nothing, so `port` is empty and curl dials 127.0.0.1:80;
  - 30 curl failures plus 30 × `sleep 1` take about 30 s;
  - the 10 s cap kills bash, and the case fails with `spawnSync /bin/bash ETIMEDOUT` (assert.ifError at :56).
- Uncapped, the step exits 1 after 30 s: "Expected a healthy daemon serving <root> on 127.0.0.1, got: no answer".
- The fail (43) and mismatch (1) cases still pass, because they exit before the new block.
- 90ed6cb5's diff touched neither this test nor any test that runs it.

EVIDENCE (HEAD bc4793cf, snapshots under /tmp, every MOE_* var cleared, Linux node 24)
- CI dry run, build-all-platforms ubuntu leg, step "Test installers with isolated profiles": exit 1. Log: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/ci/j4/07-installers.log
    ✖ Docker CI smoke match has exit 0 (10006.305826ms)
    ℹ tests 71 / ℹ pass 34 / ℹ fail 1 / ℹ skipped 36
    AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: ifError got unwanted exception: spawnSync /bin/bash ETIMEDOUT
        at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///.../scripts/tests/runtime-requirements.test.mjs:56:12)
- Before and after, from /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/mine/docker-smoke-repro.sh (a minimal git-archive per rev; logs in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/ci/docker-smoke/):
  - 291a34e3^: all 3 Docker CI smoke cases pass (match in 24 ms).
  - 291a34e3: match ✖ after 10006 ms.
  - bc4793cf: match ✖ after 10005 ms.
  - The uncapped match-mode step at bc4793cf gives status=1 after 30 s. Its stderr ends "curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 80 ... | Expected a healthy daemon serving ... got: no answer".
- The CI step has no `if:`, so it runs on the ubuntu, windows (Git Bash) and macos legs, and the 30 s loop is the same on each.

FIX DIRECTION
- Make the test model the whole step again. docker.yml's checks stay as they are.
- Simplest: PATH-first stubs in the test's bin dir:
  - `docker run -d` prints a container id;
  - `docker port` prints `127.0.0.1:<n>`;
  - a `curl` stub answers `{"status":"healthy","projectPath":"<cwd>"}` in match mode;
  - `docker inspect` prints a trivially passing command, and `docker exec`, `docker logs` and `docker rm` exit 0.
- An in-process HTTP server cannot answer while spawnSync blocks the event loop. If you want a real server, run it as a child process, or switch the case to async spawn.
- Add negative cases for the new block, so removing or breaking it turns the test red:
  - /health never answers: the step exits 1 with "Expected a healthy daemon";
  - /health reports another projectPath: the step exits 1.
- Keep each case's timeout well above its real runtime. Do not raise it to swallow the 30-try loop.

FILES: scripts/tests/runtime-requirements.test.mjs only. Not held by any open row (lanes.js -v at 09:12Z).
PLACEMENT: no dependsOn. No open row edits this file or .github/workflows/docker.yml.
definitionOfDone: `node --test scripts/tests/runtime-requirements.test.mjs` exits 0 in a Linux git-archive snapshot of the fix commit with every MOE_* var unset, and every "Docker CI smoke" case finishes in under 5 s.

New cases make the replayed Test Docker image step exit 1 when the stubbed /health never answers and when it reports another projectPath; restoring docker.yml's step to its 291a34e3^ text (no health block) makes at least one of them fail.

The row's diff leaves .github/workflows/docker.yml unchanged, and the CI step command `node --test scripts/tests/installers.test.mjs scripts/tests/install-dependencies-windows.test.mjs scripts/tests/dependencies.test.mjs scripts/tests/runtime-requirements.test.mjs` exits 0 in that snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
NEGATIVE CASES (DoD 2). Same file, same editing-tool rule.

The case table has rows of [mode, the step's exit code, text the combined stdout+stderr must contain]. Use exactly these 7 rows. The first three titles stay byte-identical:
['fail', 43, []],
['mismatch', 1, ['Expected daemon version', 'got: not-the-package-version']],
['match', 0, ['healthy: ', 'image HEALTHCHECK passed']],
['no-health', 1, ['Expected a healthy daemon serving', 'got: no answer']],
['other-project', 1, ['Expected a healthy daemon serving', '"projectPath":"/elsewhere"']],
['unhealthy', 1, ['Expected a healthy daemon serving', '"status":"starting"']],
['healthcheck-fails', 3, ['healthy: ']]

After `assert.equal(result.status, exitCode, output)`:
- assert every listed text with output.includes;
- for every mode except match, assert the output does NOT contain 'image HEALTHCHECK passed'. Only match may reach the step's end.

Each negative row fails the step for its own reason, never the version check:
- no-health exercises the 30-try loop and the empty-answer path;
- other-project and unhealthy each exercise one clause of the node check;
- healthcheck-fails (exit 3: inspect returns 'exit 3', and exec runs `sh -c 'exit 3'`) exercises the HEALTHCHECK line.

With docker.yml's step restored to its 291a34e3^ text, the step ends after the version check and exits 0. Then match, no-health, other-project, unhealthy and healthcheck-fails all fail. This was measured at plan time on Linux and on Windows.
implementationPlan.note: 7-row case table, includes assertions and no-HEALTHCHECK guard for non-match modes (written with step 1's edit).

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the last step. Load adversarial-self-review, then check:

7. Concurrent runs cannot collide: there is no temp dir and no listening port (49153 is only a string), so parallel node --test files are safe.
8. The comment above smokeStubs states both Windows reasons.
Fix anything you find. If the file changed, re-run the joined checkRefs so the evidence is fresh.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected: PATH-first stubs for docker, curl and sleep (the hunt's FIX DIRECTION). Under Git for Windows' bin/bash.exe, /mingw64/bin and /usr/bin come before any PATH node passes. At plan time, `type -P` resolved curl to /mingw64/bin/curl and sleep to /usr/bin/sleep, so those stubs would never run on the windows-latest leg. The no-health loop would also cost 60 process spawns.
Rejected: re-prepending the stub dir through BASH_ENV (mem:gotcha-git-bash-stub-path-and-msys-sparse). It works, but it needs a POSIX spelling of the temp dir and more moving parts.
Rejected: a real HTTP server as a child process. It needs async spawn or a helper process plus a free port, and the no-answer case would still need a sleep stub.
Rejected: stubbing seq to shorten the loop. That distorts the step under test.
Chosen: shell functions prepended to the step's text. There are no PATH games and no extra processes, the behaviour is identical on all three OSes, and the temp dir goes away.
The gate is three checkRefs because each checkRef is capped at 1000 characters.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: docker.yml's job runs only on ubuntu (pull_request), but runtime-requirements.test.mjs replays its run block on every build-all-platforms leg (ci.yml:240-241). Git Bash converts an env value that looks like a POSIX path when it execs a native program: EXPECTED=$PWD reaches node.exe as D:/..., the same spelling `pwd -W` prints. A JSON value starting with { is left alone, so HEALTH keeps the stub's text. node.exe launched from WSL receives only WSLENV-listed vars, so the Windows probe gets no MOE_* var. The step's EXIT trap calls docker logs and docker rm, which the docker stub models as no-ops. An unbuilt git archive is enough for CI's 4-file command: no dist or node_modules is needed (HEAD: 71 tests, 34 pass, 1 fail, which is this bug). HEAD's file also times out under Windows Git Bash, so the windows-latest leg is red as well.
planningNotes.risks: macOS runs /bin/bash 3.2: keep the stubs free of bash 4 syntax. Inside the JS template literal, a `${` would interpolate and a backslash would be eaten, so the vetted stub uses neither. On Windows, CRLF checkouts are safe: the test normalizes docker.yml, and template literals normalize CRLF to LF. QA rerunning the checkRefs from the control checkout after landing: checkRef 1's docker.yml check is vacuous there, because merge-base equals HEAD. Check `git diff --stat <completion>^ <completion>` instead; it must list only the test file. Something listening on 127.0.0.1:49153 cannot matter, because curl is a function. A future docker.yml change that calls a new docker subcommand now fails this test immediately as 'docker stub: unexpected docker ...' (exit 97) instead of timing out: that is intended.
